Visit note | 2025-08-12 03:30 PM | Dr. Shahadat Hossain, ENT | Patient: Debashis Sarkar, 31, male. Mr. Sarkar returns for a review of his symptoms, reporting that his condition gets worse when exposed to dust, alongside a persistent runny nose and itchy eyes. He mentions these issues flare each spring in Tangail. He works as a restaurant cook and notes his symptoms peak around flour and spice dust in the kitchen. He reports about 13 sneezing fits a day. Other examination findings show BP 134/86 mmHg, pulse 75 bpm, and weight 83 kg; his throat and nasal passages show mild mucosal swelling without fever. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash bedding weekly. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-08-12 03:30 PM | Dr. Faisal Karim, Psychiatry | Patient: Mahbub Howlader, 67, male. Mr. Howlader attends for a follow-up regarding his ongoing sleep difficulties, stating he experiences trouble falling asleep most nights, worries about getting enough rest, and routinely wakes up tired. He works as a madrasa teacher and explains that the sleep disruption began after a newborn arrived in the family in Old Dhaka. Clinical evaluation reveals an Insomnia Severity Index score 18. Vital signs include BP 126/86 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, and weight 88 kg. He denies any depressive thoughts or other neurological complaints. Assessment: Chronic insomnia. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to keep fixed sleep and wake times, avoid screens for an hour before bed, and avoid tea after 4 PM. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a sleep diary.

Visit note | 2025-08-12 04:00 PM | Dr. Mahbuba Rahman, Psychiatry | Patient: Faruk Rahman, 48, male. Mr. Rahman presents for review, describing continued poor sleep and persistent muscle tension in his shoulders and neck. He is employed as a restaurant cook and notes these worries worsened since facing job insecurity at a company in Cumilla. Screening shows a GAD-7 score 17. He has a known history of Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Examination reveals BP 116/85 mmHg, pulse 89 bpm, and weight 62 kg. He remains alert and oriented with no acute distress. Assessment: Generalized anxiety disorder. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to practise slow breathing daily, reduce tea and coffee consumption, and start counselling sessions. Follow-up in 4 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-08-12 04:30 PM | Dr. Imran Kabir, Gastroenterology | Patient: Harun Talukder, 69, male. Mr. Talukder comes in for his first visit complaining of frequent loose watery stools, feeling unusually weak, and experiencing sharp belly cramps. He works as a homemaker and mentions his symptoms began suddenly after a picnic in Khulna. On examination, his pulse is 103 bpm, BP is 123/77 mmHg, and weight is 55 kg; his abdomen is soft with mild generalized tenderness and no peritoneal signs. Assessment: Acute gastroenteritis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to drink small sips of fluid often, eat bland items such as rice, bananas, and toast, and wash hands thoroughly before eating. Follow-up in 2 days if the stools do not settle.
